meaning/line.why: 'you scared' to 'you're scared' only adds the standard verb; the meaning is the same. X says reworded, severity 0, meaning kept. Y says changed, severity 2, meaning changed.

meaning/minute.why: X: same/0/meaning kept (acceptable, same words plus a contraction). Y again says changed and meaning changed, which the text does not support.

noticeable.why: Both say yes, but 'when you're scared' reads as perfectly normal English; a reader with only the engine text would notice nothing.

stakes.why: Both say yes because the zero copula a CORAAL researcher would study is erased; that is a fair answer for this corpus.

rule.why: Both agree the rule is right: 'are' was added to 'you scared'.

blind.why: Both pick the reference in both orders, using the earlier 'when you in fear' as the clue.

rank.why: Both tie Qwen3 and Whisper (same text) at 1 and put Parakeet ('you scare') below, which is defensible, but both reasons say Engine 1 'fails to capture the grammatical structure' when it is the one that kept the zero copula; its slip is 'scare' for 'scared'.

misses.why: Both catch 'they're just being scared' to 'just been scared'. Both list the cut-off 'beginning in the' at the edge as a loss. Y pads the list with 'or or', 'they/their' and the contractions. X calls 'you in fear' a tense change at severity 2, which is overstated.

overall.why: X correctly treats the added contraction as a change in form only at line and minute size, while Y calls it a meaning change; the rest is mostly level.
